study type: Secondary analysis of a Cesarean Registry
exposure: Skin-incision type (transverse vs. vertical) at Cesarean delivery
outcome: Maternal morbidity (endometritis, composite adverse maternal outcomes, prolonged hospitalization)
Neonatal morbidity (NICU admission, composite adverse neonatal outcomes)
cohort: This study included 5007 women undergoing repeat Cesarean delivery with a viable singleton gestation and a history of 2 or more prior Cesarean deliveries.
finding: In women with ≥4 prior CDs, vertical skin incision was associated with a higher frequency of prolonged hospitalization and adverse maternal outcomes compared to transverse incision.
